edge.title: The number you say first
edge.setup: An interview goes well. HR asks your current CTC and your expectation. Whatever you answer becomes the ceiling of everything that follows — and you're being asked before you know what the role is budgeted at.
edge.tell: You're being asked to price yourself before you know what the buyer budgeted.
move: Deflect once, politely: 'I'd like to understand the scope first — what range is budgeted for this role?' Asking costs nothing and often works.
If pressed, give a researched range for the role and market, not your current salary. Your past pay is a fact about your last employer, not about this job.
Karnataka has no salary-history ban, so you may have to answer eventually — but 'eventually' after you've heard their number is a different conversation.
Negotiate the whole package: notice period, joining bonus, level, WFH days. Single-number fights are the easiest to lose.
edge.why: This is anchoring. The first number stated pulls every subsequent number toward it, even when both sides know it's arbitrary. Street smarts in a salon or a showroom and street smarts in an HR call are the same skill wearing different clothes.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'what's your budget?' from any contractor, the first quote at a furniture shop, a landlord asking what you currently pay.

lens.name: Principal–agent problem
lens.one_line: The person acting for you is paid for something subtly different from what you want.
lens.detail: A broker is paid when a deal closes, not when you choose well. An insurance agent is paid on commission, which differs by product. A contractor is paid for the job, not for the job lasting. None of this requires bad intent — the incentive is enough. Knowing the pay structure predicts the advice better than knowing the person.
elsewhere: Fund managers judged quarterly take risks that look fine quarterly.
A politician's horizon is the next election; infrastructure's horizon is thirty years.
A mechanic paid per part replaced finds more parts to replace.
lens.test: Before weighing advice, ask: what exactly triggers this person getting paid?
lens.today: Deccan Herald reports the BDA spent Rs 9.5 crore on the Nadaprabhu Kempegowda event and a road launch. I only have the headline, not the break-up, but the model asks the right question: an agency is rewarded for visible launches and announcements, while you want the unglamorous outcome, a road that works and a title that is clean. Weigh a promise by what the announcer is paid or praised for, not by the size of the ceremony.

moved.what: Construction World reports PM Modi will inaugurate Namma Metro's Pink Line on November 13, taking the network to 103.6 km.
moved.so_what: Expect heavy security and traffic around the inauguration on the 13th; the headlines do not say when public service starts, so check BMRCL's announcement before changing your commute.

moved.what: The Times of India reports Karnataka says oil companies blended up to 31.2% ethanol in petrol and wants consumers to have a choice of E10, E20, E30 and pure petrol; The Siasat Daily says ethanol-free Speed 100 at Rs 169/L is finding buyers in Bengaluru.
moved.so_what: Check your vehicle manual for its fuel specification before deciding whether paying for ethanol-free petrol is worth it; the premium is certain, the benefit for your vehicle is not.

moved.what: NEWSTRAIL reports a bus fare hike is straining residents' wallets.
moved.so_what: I only have the headline, not the new fares, so re-cost your monthly commute against a pass or the metro before the next recharge rather than assuming the old budget holds.

moved.what: A Karnataka consumer panel ordered the postal department to pay Rs 1.15 lakh with 6% interest to a woman whose Rs 1 lakh senior citizens' scheme deposit from 2023 was allegedly misappropriated by a postmaster who fled (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Keep the receipt and get every deposit entered and stamped in your passbook at the counter; that paper is what wins a claim later.

moved.what: ThePrint and the Times of India report the CM said the BDA will offer a land ownership guarantee to over 1 lakh residents under an amended law, with a cut in the regularisation fee.
moved.so_what: If your site sits in a BDA area with a documentation gap, ask the BDA directly about eligibility and the new fee; do not pay any agent who claims to have a shortcut.

carry_over.prompt: You are in a packed festival ground with one known gate and a temporary stage; what is your test for whether you are standing in a bottleneck?
carry_over.answer: If you cannot point to two exits without crossing the thickest part of the crowd, you are standing in a bottleneck.

quiz.question: On which date will the Pink Line be inaugurated, according to Construction World?
quiz.why: Construction World reports the inauguration on November 13.

quiz.question: To what total length will Namma Metro grow with the Pink Line?
What price per litre was reported for ethanol-free Speed 100 in Bengaluru?
What highest ethanol blend in petrol did the Karnataka minister say oil companies used?
quiz.why: The Times of India reports up to 31.2%.

quiz.question: What interest rate did the consumer panel order on the Rs 1 lakh post office deposit?
quiz.why: The Times of India reports payment of Rs 1.15 lakh with 6% interest.
